title: Ostrevia (India): clean package insert and labels
about: A Schedule H new drug: the package insert in the CDSCO format, the carton and the strip, with the red-box caution, the Rx symbol, Rule 96 particulars and the MRP.

fixed.header: For the use of a Registered Medical Practitioner or a Hospital or a Laboratory only.

blocks.text: Lumiravostat Tablets 10 mg / 25 mg
Each film-coated tablet contains: Lumiravostat 10 mg (or 25 mg). Excipients q.s. Colour: Titanium Dioxide IP (25 mg: Iron Oxide Yellow).
Film-coated tablets, 10 mg and 25 mg.
Lumiravostat is indicated for the treatment of adults with moderate to severe chronic hand eczema not adequately controlled with potent topical corticosteroids, or when these are not advisable.

10 mg orally once daily, with or without food. The dose may be increased to 25 mg once daily if the response is inadequate after 12 weeks. Hepatic impairment: 10 mg once daily in moderate impairment; not recommended in severe impairment. With strong CYP3A4 inhibitors: 10 mg once daily.
Hypersensitivity to lumiravostat or any excipient. Active tuberculosis or active serious infection. Pregnancy.

subs.title: Special warnings and precautions for use

blocks.text: Serious infections, including tuberculosis, pneumonia, cellulitis and herpes zoster, have been reported. Screen for latent tuberculosis before starting treatment. Interrupt treatment if a serious infection develops.

Malignancy, including lymphoma and non-melanoma skin cancer, and venous thromboembolism have been reported. Monitor lymphocyte and neutrophil counts, haemoglobin and liver enzymes at baseline, at 4 weeks and every 3 months.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase exposure (use 10 mg once daily). Strong CYP3A4 inducers such as rifampicin reduce exposure; avoid concomitant use.

subs.title: Use in special populations (such as pregnant women, lactating women, paediatric patients, geriatric patients etc.)

blocks.text: Pregnancy: contraindicated; women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 weeks after the last dose. Lactation: do not breastfeed during treatment and for 4 days after the last dose. Paediatric patients: safety and efficacy not established. Geriatric patients: no dose adjustment.

subs.title: Effects on ability to drive and use machines

blocks.text: No or negligible influence.
Very common: nasopharyngitis. Common: headache, nausea, acne, herpes zoster, lymphopenia, neutropenia, ALT increased. Uncommon: pneumonia, cellulitis, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism.
Reporting of suspected adverse reactions: report to the marketer, or to the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI) through the ADR reporting form or helpline.
No specific antidote. Monitor and give supportive treatment.
Lumiravostat is a reversible inhibitor of the fictional STRK1 kinase.
Dose-dependent reductions in markers of skin inflammation within 2 weeks.
Peak concentrations at 1 to 2 hours; half-life about 16 hours; metabolised mainly by CYP3A4.
Not genotoxic. Embryo-fetal toxicity in rats and rabbits at exposures close to human exposure.
10 mg: white, round, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" and "10". 25 mg: yellow, oval, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" and "25".
Not applicable.
36 months.
Alu-Alu strip of 10 tablets; carton of 3 strips.
Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture. Keep out of reach of children.

Tell patients that lumiravostat can lower the ability to fight infections, including tuberculosis, and to report fever, cough or weight loss. Advise them to seek help for leg swelling, chest pain or breathlessness, to use contraception, and not to breastfeed.

change.title: CDSCO directive: TB screening, Schedule H2, revised price

notice.from: CDSCO (fictional letter after a Subject Expert Committee meeting)
notice.title: Directive: tuberculosis screening wording, Schedule H2 inclusion and revised price
notice.text: Following the recommendation of the Subject Expert Committee (fictional), all holders of permission for lumiravostat tablets shall, within 30 days, revise the package insert to state in 4.4 that patients must be screened for latent tuberculosis with an interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) or tuberculin skin test, and a chest X-ray, before starting treatment, and add matching counselling in section 9. Separately, the brand has been added to Schedule H2 (fictional notification): the label must carry a QR code with the data elements of Schedule H2. The ceiling price has been revised (fictional NPPA order): the MRP becomes ₹ 3,600.00 for 30 tablets (₹ 1,200.00 per strip of 10).
